## Recall · Lecture 12

a) Which condition is the same as !(p && q)?
b) How many rows does a decision table with 4 conditions have?
c) Which rule runs when two rules of an else-if chain are true?

::: {.answer}
a) !p || !q
b) 16
c) the first one from the top
:::

## Activity 1 · Words to conditions · 10 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Harvest Bot is a farm robot with the facts b (battery low), f (basket full), p (ripe crop), d (dry soil), r (rain) and n (night).
- **Do it:** Write "the bot waters when the soil is dry and it is not raining" and "the bot picks a ripe crop, unless it is night".
- Then write !(d && !r) without a NOT in front of the brackets.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/rule-words.png)
:::
::::

## Check 1 · Words to conditions

Which conditions are right?

::: {.reveal}
1. The bot waters with d && !r.
2. The bot picks with p && !n, because "unless n" means "if not n".
3. De Morgan turns !(d && !r) into !d || r.
:::

## Activity 2 · The decision table · 12 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The designer says: home if b, otherwise pick if p, otherwise water if d, otherwise wait.
- **Do it:** Make the 8-row table of b, p and d with the action of each row.
- How many rows has each action, and is the table complete?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/decision-table.png)
:::
::::

## Check 2 · The decision table

How many rows has each action?

::: {.reveal}
1. The bot goes home in the 4 rows with b = T.
2. With b = F, it picks in 2 rows, waters in 1 row and waits in 1 row.
3. Every row has one action, so the table is complete and has no conflict.
:::

## Activity 3 · Order and clean · 10 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The code is if (p) Pick(); else if (b) Home(); else if (d && !b) Water(); else Wait();
- **Do it:** Test the row b = T, p = T, d = F. What does the chain do, and what does the designer want?
- Then write the chain in the right order.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/rule-order.png)
:::
::::

## Check 3 · Order and clean

What is wrong, and what is the fix?

::: {.reveal}
1. The chain picks, but the designer wants Home, because the battery is low.
2. The right chain starts with if (b) Home(), then Pick, Water and Wait.
3. The Water rule then needs only d, because b is always false there.
:::

## Activity 4 · Edge cases · 12 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The rule says the battery is low under 20 %, but the code says battery <= 20.
- **Do it:** Which value of the battery finds the bug?
- Then write four edge-case tests for "sell with at least 50 apples and fewer than 3 trips".
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/edge-cases.png)
:::
::::

## Check 4 · Edge cases

Which tests find the bugs?

::: {.reveal}
1. Battery = 20 finds the bug, and the fix is battery < 20.
2. The sell rule is apples >= 50 && trips < 3.
3. Good tests are (50, 2) sell, (49, 2) no, (50, 3) no and (51, 2) sell.
:::

## Game challenge · The guard of Torch Hall

{{< sim file="sims/guard-brain.html" poster="sims/guard-brain.png" title="Guard Brain: rules, order and the decision table" task="The designer of Torch Hall adds an alarm rule to the guard: it runs to the bell when it hears the alarm, unless it is weak. **Show:** the 8 rows without the alarm in Guard Brain. **Ask:** where does the new rule go in the chain?" >}}

## Try it · The new rule set (harder)

The facts: the guard flees when weak (health under 30). It runs to the bell when it hears the alarm, unless it is weak. The alarm beats the player.

a) How many rows does the new decision table have?
b) Where does the bell rule go in the chain?
c) Which health value finds the bug in the code health <= 30?

::: {.answer}
a) 16
b) after Flee, before Attack
c) health = 30
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can write the rules of a game in words as conditions.
- You can make the decision table of a rule set and check that it is complete.
- You can put the rules of an else-if chain in the right order.
- You can test a number rule at its border with edge cases.
